output.summary: KEP-3458 proposes that the KCCM service controller stop adding/removing Nodes from load balancer node sets when a Node becomes NotReady/Ready or gets the ToBeDeletedByClusterAutoscaler taint, gated behind a new StableLoadBalancerNodeSet feature gate. The status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Removing a Node from the load balancer node set during transient readiness or termination instantly kills its connections, preventing connection draining. Frequent load balancer re-syncs also cause excessive cloud API calls that can trigger rate limiting. The KEP stops re-syncing the node set in these cases to enable draining and reduce API calls.

alternatives.option: Keep re-configuring the load balancer node set on Ready/NotReady and taint changes
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this removal terminates connections instantly and causes excessive cloud provider update calls, which the KEP aims to fix.

alternatives.option: Change health checks to drain connections while a Node is draining
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists enabling connection draining while a Node is draining as a non-goal because it requires health check changes.

alternatives.option: Also stop re-configuring for fully deleted or newly added nodes, or nodes annotated exclude-from-external-load-balancers
alternatives.why_not: The readme lists these as non-goals; the KEP does not change that behavior.

evidence.quote: this KEP proposes that the service controller stops synchronizing the load balancer node set in these cases
a new feature gate `StableLoadBalancerNodeSet` will be introduced, which will be used to enable the more optimal behavior
removing the Node in question from the load balancers' node set will cause all connections on that node to get terminated instantly
re-syncing load balancers like this can lead to rate-limiting by the cloud provider due to an excessive amount of update calls
